Subject: PII handling: prompts & outputs - confirmation and retention

Hi Lydia / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:
- Acme will send customer-provided prompts and customer identifiers to Redwood for inference via the Hosted API.
- Key concerns: whether raw prompts and model outputs are stored, where they are stored (region/residency), how long they are retained, and whether they are used for model training.
- Acme needs an answer to those items to progress procurement and get security sign-off.

Next steps I promised:
1) Loop in our privacy/security lead to confirm default behavior and available contractual controls.
2) Share our short summary + retention matrix (attached).
3) Book a follow-up call with your security team if needed.

See attached: PII_Data_Retention_Table.pdf

Neha — can you confirm the bullets below and add any contractual options we should call out? I marked the items we discussed.

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Lydia / Tom —

Thanks for the questions. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's default behavior and the contractual options available for enterprise customers. I've attached a short summary and our SOC2 checklist for your security team.

Default (Hosted API):
- What we store by default:
  - Request metadata (timestamp, request ID, client IP hashed, route/model requested). Retention: 365 days.
  - Full prompts and model outputs: retained for 30 days by default for debugging, abuse detection, and support. Retention can be configured per-account.
- Training usage:
  - Redwood does NOT use customer prompts/outputs to train our public models by default. For Hosted customers, we may use anonymized aggregated telemetry to improve service quality; any use of customer content for model training requires explicit contractual opt-in.
- Data residency:
  - Hosted production data is stored in the AWS region tied to your account; we can enforce US-only residency (us-east-1 or us-west-2) under enterprise contract. Private/Dedicated deployments keep data in customer VPC.
- KV cache / in-memory artifacts:
  - Per-request KV cache and ephemeral model state are not persisted beyond the request lifecycle unless the customer chooses to persist results.
- Access controls & encryption:
  - Data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private.
- Audit & logs:
  - Admin audit logs and access records available; we can provide delivery of audit logs to your SIEM via S3 or syslog on contract.

Enterprise contractual options:
- Option A (Standard Enterprise): disable use of content for training; set prompt/output retention to 0 days (no content persisted), retain only metadata for 180 days.
- Option B (Retention + Residency): US-only residency + custom retention windows (e.g., metadata 365 days, content 7 days).
- Option C (Private/Dedicated): deploy Redwood Private in your VPC — we do not store prompts/outputs in our control plane; customer controls storage and retention.

Attachments: Redwood_PII_Handling_Summary.pdf (short doc with the above + data flow diagram), SOC2-Compliance-Checklist.xlsx

If you'd like, we can run through the attached summary on a 30-min call with your security team next week. Rishi / Marissa — please propose two slots.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
